question.value: Does the massive star-forming region IRAS 12326-6245 host an explosive outflow (streamers with Hubble-Lemaitre-like expansion), and what are its age, energy and the implied Galactic event rate?

evidence.quote: Here, we report one more explosive outflow related with the massive and bright star-forming region IRAS 12326$-$6245 using Band 6 sensitive and high angular resolution ($\sim$0.2$''$) Atacama Large Millimeter/Submillimeter Array (ALMA) observations.
The observations were carried out during the Cycle 4 science data program 2016.1.01347.S (PI: Silvia Leurini) in 2017 July 20
using Band 6 sensitive and high angular resolution ($\sim$0.2$''$)

findings_qualitative.value: Over 10 CO streamers with Hubble-like expansion point to center of a newly found dusty shell

evidence.quote: We find over 10 molecular and collimated well-defined streamers, with Hubble-Lemaitre like expansion motions

claims.experiment: ALMA 12CO(2-1) streamer mapping and velocity-distance plot
claims.result: 10 streamers pointing to shell center with linear velocity-distance relation
claims.finding: A new explosive outflow, age ~700 yr, energy 1e48 erg

evidence.quote: This outflow therefore adds one more case to the list of the explosive outflows

claims.hypothesis: Explosive events occur at a rate comparable to massive star formation
claims.finding: Similar to massive star formation and supernova rates

evidence.quote: Our rough estimate will be refined once more explosive outflows will be detected.

limitations_admitted.value: Explosion center uncertain due to few streamers

evidence.quote: we were not able to do a more complete statistical analysis to find the sky center of the explosion due to the low number of explosive streamers

limitations_admitted.value: Mass is a lower limit since CO likely optically thick

evidence.quote: more likely the emission is optically thick at these millimeter wavelengths, so this estimation should be considered a lower limit
